findings.reason: without a discriminating arm the gate passes on the wrong field the paragraph names, so the defect it would expose ships unmeasured.
findings.text: the added arm "A waiter on a section whose plan's `depends_on` names an unshipped plan stays `awaiting-upstream`" is satisfied by any of three readings of the row — the `depends_on` rows with `satisfied` false, the composite `dependency_ready`, or the row's `ready` — because an unshipped dependency makes all three false (reckon/roadmap.py:3359-3361, 3438-3448); the arm therefore cannot show that the mechanism reads the `depends_on` answer, and no arm covers a section the roadmap reports ready under a plan whose only open decision is scoped to another section.

findings.reason: the sentence names the wrong field for the test it claims to make, so the shared predicate would answer a plan-level summary instead of the per-section reading the same paragraph requires, and the added done-when arm cannot tell the two apart.
findings.text: §8 defines `dependency_ready` as the field that "answers the plan's `depends_on`", but it is computed as `"dependency_ready": is_ready` (reckon/roadmap.py:3540, copied onto section rows at :3750), and `is_ready` (:3438-3448) is the conjunction of dispatchable, authorised, no plan dependency, no explicit/held/gate blocker, no plan-holding decision, not a cycle member and not closable — it is the row's plan-level summary verdict, identical to `ready` (:3531), which the same paragraph has just forbidden a wait to read ("A wait is answered per section, never from the plan-level summary"). The field that answers a plan's `depends_on` is `depends_on` itself (:3514), the dependency rows whose `satisfied` is computed at :3356-3361. A worker following the sentence implements the predicate against the summary the paragraph forbids and leaves the `depends_on` rows unread.

findings.reason: a predicate built from this list over-holds sections the roadmap reports ready, so queued work stalls on a decision the plan intends to scope to one section.
findings.text: §8 lists `decision_blockers` among the fields the per-section predicate reads, but that row list is every decision in state `open` or `gated` (reckon/roadmap.py:3389, reported at :3527), including the section-scoped decisions the roadmap deliberately keeps out of the plan verdict (`plan_holding_decisions`, :3385, feeds `is_ready`/`is_blocked` at :3445/:3455) and the `gated` ones the adjacent comment says "never blocks the plan's own execution"; the section-scoped wait reaches the section through `section_readiness`'s blockers instead (:3586-3603). Reading `decision_blockers` per section would hold every section of a plan whose open decision is scoped to a different section, diverging from the roadmap derivation §8 says it reuses rather than restates, and would leave those sections `awaiting-upstream` with no arm in the done-when to show it.
